secondary-foreground-strong.$description: fix7 (P1-2/P1-14 gate blocker, UX round 6): accessible TEXT alias for Badge's `secondary` variant, distinct from `secondary-foreground`. The generic enum dot-chip (`ReadEnum`'s fallback branch — every 'Maintenance Type'/'Issue Type'/'Vehicle Type' chip in the product, one shared code path per P1-14) renders `text-secondary-foreground` (#0072d6) on `bg-secondary` (#e6f2fc) at 4.22:1, short of WCAG AA 4.5:1 — universal, every card/list/detail surface that shows one of these chips. Aliases info-scale.700 (#00478a, an existing ramp step, same hue family as secondary/primary): measured 8.14:1 on secondary (#e6f2fc) — comfortable headroom, well clear of 4.5:1. Deliberately a NEW role slot, not an edit to `secondary-foreground` itself: that token is also Button's secondary-variant text and other non-chip consumers, none of which this finding named or measured. `color.dark.secondary-foreground-strong` below is a literal, not this same alias — dark theme's `secondary`/`secondary-foreground` pairing is a completely different pair of colors (dark gray fill, near-white text, already ~10:1 per that token's own docblock), so the dark mirror simply reuses the already-passing `dark.secondary-foreground` value rather than forcing this light-theme-specific navy onto a dark background it was never measured against.

muted-foreground-strong.$description: fix7 (A7 gate blocker): accessible field-LABEL role, distinct from `muted-foreground`. Several `FieldGrid`/section-renderer label call sites (`emphasis="strong"`, the identity-panel key-facts list, tile labels) were hardcoded to `text-gray-400` (#98a2b3) citing a Figma spec — but #98a2b3 on `background`/`card` measures 2.46:1, a WCAG AA blocker (A7). This run's rule is 'Figma wins on look, UX heuristics win on behavior'; legibility is behavior. Aliases gray.600 (#475467); measured ~7.36:1 on `background` (#f9fafb), ~7.69:1 on `card` (#ffffff) — both clear 4.5:1 with generous headroom. Deliberately a NEW role slot, not an edit to gray.400 itself: other consumers legitimately keep gray-400's current value, and `color.dark.muted-foreground` below depends on the literal #98a2b3 clearing contrast where IT sits.

input.$description: Input BORDER (shadcn --input convention). Figma binds Grey-300 to text-field outlines (login spec) — one step darker than the generic `border` so fields read as fields.

ring.$description: Focus-ring color — PRIMARY, not primary-50 (fix3): the :focus-visible ring must be visible on white surfaces (WCAG 2.4.7 / UX-NOTES 'ring 2px primary'); #e6f2fc was invisible (1.09:1 vs white). Dark theme already used primary.

success-text.$description: D-6 (filters SPEC I.80): accessible TEXT alias for brand green — `success` (#12b76a, 2.62:1 on white) and the Figma-drawn #22c882 (2.18:1 on white) both fail WCAG 4.5:1 as text and must never be used for `Select All` / `Selected to Top` / a create-CTA label. Aliases success-scale.700 (#027a48); measured 5.41:1 on color.card (#ffffff), 5.18:1 on color.background (#f9fafb) — both clear 4.5:1. Fills (checkbox, `Available` badge, chip) are untouched and keep the drawn hex; this token is TEXT-only.

error-text.$description: D-6 (filters SPEC I.80): accessible TEXT alias for the destructive red used as text (`Clear all` / `Unselect All` / the clear `×` glyph) — kept distinct from the singleton `destructive`/`destructive-emphasis` fill slots. Aliases error.700 (#b42318); measured 6.57:1 on color.card (#ffffff), 6.29:1 on color.background (#f9fafb) — both clear 4.5:1.

warning-text.$description: fix7 (job-orders gate blocker): accessible TEXT alias for the warning amber used as text — same D-6 job as `success-text`/`error-text` above, added because no equivalent existed for `warning`. `warning` (#f79009) measures 2.35:1 on white at body-text size — a WCAG AA blocker found on the Preventive Maintenance list's 'Due Today' `SignedNumberView` cell (`zeroTone: "warning"` resolving through `@fams/v5-composer`'s `TONE_TEXT_CLASS`, the same class of defect `error-text` already fixed for `danger`). Deliberately NOT a new ramp value: aliases the EXISTING warning-scale.700 (#b54708, already used ad hoc as text-safe amber elsewhere — `RouteJobCard`, `KpiMetricCard`, `CockpitAlert`) so this token gives that established convention a name instead of inventing a parallel one. Measured (`contrast-lib.mjs`): 5.43:1 on color.card (#ffffff), 5.19:1 on color.background (#f9fafb) — both clear 4.5:1. Fills/borders/icon glyphs (Badge's `warning` variant, `IconBadge`, the tone dot) are untouched and keep the drawn `warning`/`warning-scale-500` hex; this token is TEXT-only.

lightest.$description: Default Text/Lightest — Gray Modern/50 (Figma DS V2).

lighter.$description: Default Text/Lighter — Gray Modern/400 (Figma DS V2).

light.$description: Default Text/Light — Gray Modern/500 (Figma DS V2).

normal.$description: Default Text/Normal — Gray Modern/600 (Figma DS V2).

dark.$description: Default Text/Dark — Gray Modern/700 (Figma DS V2).

darker.$description: Default Text/Darker — Gray Modern/800 (Figma DS V2).

darkest.$description: Default Text/Darkest — Gray Modern/900 (Figma DS V2).

chart-heat.$description: Magnitude (not categorical) heat scales. `0` is the reserved NO-DATA swatch — deliberately out of family (neutral grey, no warm hue) so an unmeasured cell never reads as a low measured value; it is always paired with a glyph, never colour alone. `low`/`mid`/`high` are the original 3-stop warm ramp kept for continuous scales. `1`–`5` are a true 5-stop discrete sequential ramp whose relative luminance decreases monotonically, so a 5-class binned scale no longer has to stretch 3 stops across 5 classes (which left the lightest measured class ~3% from the no-data swatch).

medal.$description: Ordinal (1st/2nd/3rd) podium decoration. A SEPARATE family from the status colours on purpose: a page that already spends red on 'worst bin' and 'negative delta' must not also spend it on 'third place'. Bronze is a real copper hue, not the error tint. `-surface` and `-accent` are FILLED GROUNDS under themed ink (`text-foreground` / `text-muted-foreground`) and therefore carry real dark overrides in `color.dark.medal-*` — the light tints sit at 1.0-1.3:1 against dark-mode foreground. The dark surfaces are luminance-matched to `color.dark.card` (#1d2939) so a podium card reads at the same contrast as any other card. `-border` is a stroke, not a ground, and is deliberately theme-neutral so 1st/2nd/3rd read as the same three metals in either theme (recorded in packages/tokens/test/theme-parity.test.js).

accent-family.$description: Non-status accent hue families (Figma 'Accent' collection) — 5 named stops each. Named accent-family (not accent) because color.accent/accent-foreground already carry the semantic role token; error/success/warning/info families are intentionally omitted here since they already exist as 9-step ramps (color.error, color.success-scale, color.warning-scale, color.info-scale).

dark.$description: Dark-mode overrides (decision #2, ruling ⑤). Emitted by the fams/dark-mode post-build action under :root[data-theme="dark"] and @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) — same variable names as the light values, not a separate flat namespace.

text-color-lightest.$description: Dark-mode mirror of Default Text scale (inverted ramp).

secondary.$description: Bug fix (consumer parity report 2026-08-22): was #1d2939, identical to dark.card — a secondary button on a card had no visible chrome until hover. Lifted to gray-700 (existing ramp step), giving ~1.41:1 luminance separation from dark.card while secondary-foreground (#f9fafb) still clears 10:1 against it.

secondary-foreground-strong.$description: fix7: dark-mode mirror for the new chip-text role (see the light `color.secondary-foreground-strong` docblock). Literal, not an alias — this file's dark section is read un-resolved by `buildDarkModeCss()`. Reuses the exact value of `color.dark.secondary-foreground` above — dark's `secondary`/`secondary-foreground` pairing already clears ~10:1 (see that token's own docblock), so no separate dark value was needed.

muted-foreground.$description: Bug fix (consumer parity report 2026-08-22): was #667085 (identical to light muted-foreground), only 2.96:1 on dark.card / 3.06:1 on dark.background — fails WCAG AA body text. Raised to gray-400 (existing ramp step): ~6.90:1 vs dark.background (#101828), ~5.71:1 vs dark.card (#1d2939).

muted-foreground-strong.$description: fix7: dark-mode mirror for the new field-label role (see the light `color.muted-foreground-strong` docblock). Literal, not an alias — this file's dark section is read un-resolved by `buildDarkModeCss()`. Reuses the exact value `color.dark.muted-foreground` above already proved safe (~5.71:1 vs dark.card, ~6.90:1 vs dark.background) rather than introducing an unverified new dark value.

success-text.$description: D-6 dark counterpart of color.success-text — equals color.success-scale.400 (written as a literal here, matching this file's dark-section convention: buildDarkModeCss() in style-dictionary.config.js reads color.dark.* directly off the raw JSON, un-resolved, so an alias string would ship as literal broken CSS). Measured 7.69:1 on color.dark.card (#1d2939), 9.28:1 on color.dark.background (#101828).

error-text.$description: D-6 dark counterpart of color.error-text — equals color.error.400 (same literal-value convention as success-text above; happens to match color.dark.destructive-emphasis's value, which is coincidental — the two slots serve different roles, text vs. emphasis fill). Measured 5.28:1 on color.dark.card (#1d2939), 6.37:1 on color.dark.background (#101828).

warning-text.$description: fix7 dark counterpart of color.warning-text — equals color.warning-scale.400 (literal, matching this file's dark-section convention: `buildDarkModeCss()` reads `color.dark.*` un-resolved, see success-text/error-text above). `warning`/`warning-scale` carry NO dark override elsewhere in this file, so the light ramp's own darkest-legible-on-white step (warning-scale.700, #b54708) would otherwise leak into dark mode at only ~2.71:1 on `color.dark.card` — a real failure this token specifically prevents. Measured 7.99:1 on color.dark.card (#1d2939), 9.64:1 on color.dark.background (#101828).

border.$description: Bug fix (consumer parity report 2026-08-22): was #667085, identical to dark.muted-foreground — a CountTabs count drawn in muted-foreground on a border-filled chip rendered at 1.00:1 (invisible). New value is a subtle step above dark.card (#1d2939, ~1.22:1 luminance separation) chosen so dark.muted-foreground (#98a2b3) still clears 4.5:1 (~4.68:1) when drawn on it.

input.$description: Bug fix (consumer parity report 2026-08-22): was #667085, identical to dark.muted-foreground (and, pre-fix, to dark.border/dark.sidebar-border) — an input's border was indistinguishable from muted text. Light ramp distinguishes input (gray-300 #d0d5dd) from border (gray-200 #eaecf0) by one ramp step, so the same relationship is mirrored here: raised to gray-600 (#475467, existing ramp step) — a distinct step beyond dark.border (#2b3749, ~1.57:1 luminance separation) and dark.secondary (#344054, ~1.36:1 separation), clearly apart from dark.muted-foreground (#98a2b3, ~2.98:1 separation). ~1.91:1 vs dark.card (#1d2939), ~2.31:1 vs dark.background (#101828) — an input outline is a UI-component boundary (WCAG 1.4.11 territory, not body text), and it now reads as a step distinctly more prominent than the generic border, matching the light-theme convention.

surface-primary.$description: Dark override for the white app surface — luminance-matched to color.dark.card so panes built on surface-primary (e.g. the login auth pane) stay coherent with dark foreground/input tokens instead of leaving a white pane under light-on-dark ink (2026-08-25 login contrast bug).

surface-minimal.$description: Dark override matching color.dark.background — used by disabled/read-only field fills.

sidebar-border.$description: Bug fix (consumer parity report 2026-08-22): was #667085, equal to both dark.muted-foreground and (pre-fix) dark.border. Now a distinct third value, a subtle step above dark.sidebar/dark.background (#101828, ~1.15:1 separation), keeping dark.muted-foreground (#98a2b3) at ~6.00:1 when drawn on it.

wall._comment: Wall-display surface — the dark, always-on operations screens (Command Center). A deliberately SEPARATE scope from the light semantic set: these surfaces are not a dark-mode variant of a light screen, they are their own always-dark canvas, so they must not flip with data-theme. Values are the ones the Command Center shipped with, moved here verbatim.

caption.$description: Shaheer ticket T-072, decision #2: platform minimum raised 10px → 12px.
Shaheer ticket T-072, decision #2: bumped proportionally with text.caption (was 12px @ 10px font).

extrabold.$description: Gilroy Extrabold — synced with Figma Design System V2's type-style matrix (Sb_heading/Display rows use it); not yet consumed by `text`/`leading` (those stop at bold).

font-size.$description: Figma Design System V2 'FontSize' scale (15 tokens, spec names verbatim, kebab-cased). ADDITIVE — a separate namespace from `text.*` (the pre-existing h1-h6/body-xl../caption scale ui-kit's Heading/Text components already consume). Where the two overlap the values agree (h1 48, h2 40, h3 32, h4 28, h5 24, h6 20) EXCEPT `caption`: this scale's Caption is 10px per Figma, while `text.caption` is deliberately 12px (Shaheer ticket T-072, decision #2 — platform accessibility minimum). Left as a DOCUMENTED CONFLICT, not resolved here — `text.caption` stays 12px; components should keep reading `text.caption`, not `font-size.caption`, until a follow-up reconciles the two (see PROGRESS.md).

caption.$description: Figma spec value. See group $description — `text.caption` (12px) is the one components should keep using; this exists for parity/documentation with the Figma token list.

line-height.$description: Figma Design System V2 'LineHeight' scale (13 tokens, spec names verbatim). ADDITIVE — separate namespace from `leading.*` (the pre-existing h1-h6/body-xl../caption line-heights `text`-scale components consume, which stay authoritative for those roles). This scale exists so the `typography.*` composite styles below can reference it by its own Figma-native names.

screen.$description: Figma Design System V2 'Responsive' max-widths — CONTAINER/canvas max-widths for the product's own responsive breakpoints (Desktop/Tablet/Mobile design frames), NOT the Tailwind `breakpoint.*` scale below. `breakpoint.*` (640/768/1024/1280/1536, Tailwind defaults) is widely assumed across ui-kit's responsive utilities (`sm:`/`md:`/`lg:`/`xl:`/`2xl:`) and is NOT replaced. `screen.*` is a distinct, additive group for consumers that need to cap a layout's width to match the Figma canvas sizes (e.g. a page shell's `max-width`) — use `max-w-[var(--screen-lg)]`-style consumption or a future `Container` component, never by re-pointing existing `sm:`/`md:`/… utilities at these values.

sm-tab.$description: Figma 'sm(tab)' — value as specified (786, not the conventional 768).

typography.$description: Composite text styles transcribed from the Figma Design System V2 'style-row' matrix (named text-style cards: Font Family / Weight / Font Size / Line Height / Letter Spacing). Modeled as GROUPED tokens (one leaf per property, `$type` matching DTCG: fontFamily/fontWeight/dimension) rather than a single composite `$value`, consistent with how this file already models every other multi-property concept (no precedent for composite `$value` tokens here) and safe for the existing `css/variables` / `tailwind/theme` formatters, which walk `dictionary.allTokens` and don't special-case a `typography` `$type`. Every leaf aliases the scale token it came from (`font-size.*` / `line-height.*` / `font-weight.*` / `font.sans`) so re-tuning a scale value flows through automatically. Coverage: every row sampled from the Figma matrix images is transcribed exactly; sizes visible in FontSize/LineHeight but not sampled as an individual style-row card (Sb_heading1/2, Body1/2, D1-D4 at weights other than the one shown) are filled in at Regular weight ONLY by the same size→line-height pairing the sampled rows established, flagged '$description: inferred' — verify against Figma before treating as design-final.

xs.$description: Elements shorter than 20px tall (Figma Design System V2).

sm.$description: Buttons/inputs/small cards, 20–48px tall (Figma Design System V2).

md.$description: Surfaces ≥48px tall — cards, modals, widgets (Figma Design System V2).

sheet.$description: Mobile sheet / bottom-sheet top corners — the large radius where a white sheet meets a brand-colored backdrop (mobile login, drawers). Deliberately its own semantic key rather than an `xl` step: `rounded-xl` is already in use from Tailwind's default scale and must not shift.

popover.$description: Floating panel/popover elevation (FilterPanel, ColumnCustomizer) — Figma Shadows/Custom/Spreaded.

popover-sm.$description: Tight anchored-popover shadow for compact identity/context popovers (UserPopover — Figma Shadows/Custom/Icon Shadow).

inline.$description: Icon-to-label, chip-to-chip. Same value as spacing.2 — semantic alias, not a new size.

field.$description: Vertical gap between form fields (Stack default gap). Same value as spacing.4.

section.$description: Gap between form sections / page regions. Same value as spacing.6.

fast.$description: Micro-interactions — hover, focus ring, checkbox toggle.

normal.$description: Default — most component state transitions (button, input, tab).

slow.$description: Larger surfaces — dialog, drawer, sheet enter/exit.

ease.$description: Timing-function curves (Material-derived). Value is a ready-to-use CSS `cubic-bezier()` string, matching this file's convention of pre-formatted CSS values (see shadow, font).

standard.$description: General-purpose — the default for most transitions.

z-index.$description: Semantic stacking scale — never a raw number at point of use (no `z-50`). Ordered so overlays/menus/toasts never collide. Emitted as `--z-index-*` (Tailwind v4's `z-*` utility namespace) with a `--z-*` alias kept for direct `var(--z-…)` consumers — see themeVarName()/isZIndexToken() in style-dictionary.config.js.

tooltip.$description: Always on top — must render above toasts.
